items.title: CVE-2026-68928 - Acode: Exported TerminalService (bundled terminal plugin) lets any installed app execute arbitrary shell commands as Acode
items.one_liner: Update Acode for Android to version 1.12.7 to fix an exported terminal service allowing arbitrary shell command execution.
items.summary: A vulnerability, CVE-2026-68928, affects Acode, an Android text and code editor, in versions 1.11.6 through 1.12.7. The bundled TerminalService is declared as an exported service without binding permissions or caller verification, allowing any local zero-permission app to send commands. Malicious apps can bind to the service and execute arbitrary shell commands inside Acode's UID via ProcessBuilder. The issue is fixed in version 1.12.7.
key_facts: CVE-2026-68928: Exported service unverified caller vulnerability in Acode
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-68928 lets any local Android app execute shell commands inside Acode's security context via an unprotectd exported service.

items.title: Dual-Axis Policy Optimization for LLM Agents: Bayesian Feedback Attribution and Trajectory Mass Normalization
items.one_liner: BATON introduces a dual-axis policy optimization framework for LLM agents combining Bayesian feedback attribution and trajectory normalization.
items.summary: Reinforcement learning optimization for LLM agents involves intra-trajectory feedback attribution and inter-trajectory objective aggregation. The authors introduce BATON (Bayesian Attribution and Trajectory Objective Normalization), a dual-axis policy optimization framework. BATON utilizes Bayesian Feedback Attribution to construct a posterior over sampled actions and Trajectory Mass Normalization to assign equal optimization mass to complete trajectories. Experiments across ALFWorld, WebShop, and SearchQA demonstrate that both axes yield independent and combined performance gains across model scales.
items.bottom_line: Decoupling intra-trajectory feedback attribution and inter-trajectory aggregation provides consistent performance improvements for reinforcement learning in LLM agents.

items.title: UnifiedPlayers: Enhance Tool-Integrated Reasoning in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.one_liner: UnifiedPlayers coordinates planning, execution, and evaluation players via GRPO to improve tool-integrated agent reasoning.
items.summary: Self-evolving tool-using agents often suffer from separated trajectory generation and static verification that reinforce shared errors. To address this coordination challenge, researchers introduce UnifiedPlayers, a cooperative framework containing a Planning Player, Execution Player, and Evaluation Player coordinated by role-specific rewards under GRPO. Tested across twelve reasoning benchmarks, UnifiedPlayers outperforms the strongest prior baseline by at least 3.5% on mathematical reasoning and 3.9% on general reasoning tasks. Furthermore, the learned verifier achieves 84.2% adversarial detection accuracy with significantly higher per-question variance.
items.bottom_line: Cooperative multi-player reinforcement learning with specialized roles significantly boosts tool-using LLM reasoning and verification.

items.title: Rethinking Multi-Agent Collaboration: When More Is Less
items.one_liner: Multi-agent systems face diminishing returns outside sparse long-horizon tasks, leading to the introduction of the SAIGE graph evolution framework.
items.summary: An analysis of multi-agent collaboration versus single-agent systems demonstrates that multi-agent setups face diminishing returns and high context overhead, conferring systematic benefits primarily in long-horizon tasks with sparse dependencies while single-agent harnesses remain superior in tightly coupled sequential workflows. To address this, researchers proposed SAIGE, a lightweight collaboration framework based on Semantic-Aware Incremental Graph Evolution that models collaboration as a dynamically evolving graph. Experiments reveal that scaling the agent pool or deepening recursion levels does not consistently improve task outcomes.
items.bottom_line: Adding more agents does not make a system more intelligent; multi-agent superiority is strictly bounded by task structure rather than being universally applicable.

claims.text: Through systematic analysis, we delineate the capability boundaries of multi-agent collaboration relative to single-agent alternatives, showing that it confers systematic benefits specifically in long-horizon tasks with sparse dependencies, while single-agent harnesses remain superior in tightly coupled, sequential workflows.
